To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the PageRank algorithm is the best choice for ranking users in Twitter, and the HITS algorithm should be avoided at all costs.

(1) the most popular algorithms for ranking Twitter users are PageRank, HITS, and EigenRank; (2) these algorithms are vulnerable to spamming; (3) the most popular methods for spam detection are the ones based on the ratio of followers to following users; (4) a simple method for desensitizing the ranking algorithms is proposed.
(1) the prestige algorithms are vulnerable to the abuse of the linking practice, and (2) a simple and effective method for desensitizing them is available.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to rank users in social networks.
the question of whether it is possible to rank users in Twitter in a way that is not vulnerable to abuse, and if so, what the most suitable algorithms are.
the problem of identifying the users with the highest rank in a social network.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no perfect algorithm for ranking users in Twitter and that there is no single best way to do it.
the most important thing to consider in the design of a prestige algorithm for a social network is the nature of the underlying network itself.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the current algorithms are vulnerable to the abuse of linking malpractice and we have provided a first step towards the solution of this problem.
the author presents an overview of the most common centrality methods, their weaknesses and their vulnerabilities to linking abuse, and he suggests a first approach to desensitize such methods.
the proposed algorithm can be considered a first step towards the development of a ranking algorithm which can withstand the effects of the most commonly used cheating techniques.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the most popular algorithms for ranking users are not robust to cheating and, therefore, their results should be taken with a grain of salt.
, although there is a plethora of algorithms that have been proposed for ranking users in a social network, they all suffer from the same vulnerability to the so-called ―nepotism problem‖.
